pullRequest.title: docs: plan portable identifier admission before ledger append
pullRequest.body:
The canonical Clio writer currently appends programmatic numeric-leading keyword identifiers that its own strict reader rejects immediately under NBB 1.4.207. This planning PR addresses [Clio issue 1](https://github.com/open-hax/clio/issues/1) through an incoming three-point card for portable identifier admission and checks at the existing writer boundary.

The plan preserves strict reading, lawful canonical hash preimages, event identity, locking and immutable ledger prefixes. Shared law fixtures precede minimal adapter changes; adjacent schema/projection writers get an explicit coverage decision. [Foresight 135](https://github.com/open-hax/foresight/issues/135) retains separate ownership of reviewed append-only corpus reconciliation. No implementation or historical data rewrite is included.

Evidence is from actual `runtime/open` / `runtime/append!` / `read-ledger` calls at current Clio `788cdd3434615a7932b924e68520dbf7f88408c2`, in private empty fixtures: both bad identifiers append then fail canonical read-back under exact NBB 1.4.207; the lawful control reads; historical NBB1.3.204 reads the same emitted bytes. Raw artifacts and hashes are retained. These observations reproduce the defect, not a repaired test pass.

The mapped personal fork and upstream main are identical. This new clone/worktree preserves source, hash protocol, reader, runtime installation and repository settings. Auto-merge is off, and no inherited/registered workflow or eager merge caller exists at this baseline. There is no configured board or existing ready card: qualified planning review and a real lawful Rheos ready event are required before implementation.

Validation: new EDN receipt parses with required keys/vector fields; both Markdown links resolve and diff check passes. Manual CodeRabbit requests are held because the current native personal account footer reports zero included reviews; automatic/pending requests remain deduplicated. Optional unavailable/quota responses supply no approval or round credit.

pullRequest.title: docs: plan lossless late-control admission for Sol turns
pullRequest.body:
Current Sol can acknowledge a streamed steer or follow-up with an already resolved nil promise, then clear controls arriving after the final drain. This full planning proposal specifies delivery or explicit rejection for every accepted control, preserving serialized turns, caller acknowledgement, history and cancellation. It implements no runtime change.

Refs https://github.com/open-hax/eta-mu/issues/255 and the exact original Eta card identity sol-turn-session-late-control-messages. All three original scope requirements and both completion criteria remain: deliberate policy for both late control kinds, a direct deterministic final-drain race fixture, no successful-looking discarded message, and complete Sol test/kondo verification. The newly authored Incoming/P2/proposed2 Sol story has a distinct UUID29ea92e6-0804-5097-badd-8985483e958e; it does not move or close the original Eta card, invent cross-board dependency identity, or claim native registration/Ready.

The plan explicitly distinguishes queue consumption from delivery. The pinned owning turn-processor may observe abort after an awaited drain has already removed controls. Proposed policy hands undelivered normal-completion controls to existing serialized turns, and explicitly refuses undelivered controls on failure/abort/refused admission. Acknowledgement timing, cross-kind ordering, cancellation, pending turns and public API compatibility require reviewed decisions. Portable .cljc laws and shaped decisions precede the existing host adapter; no copied runner or second event/board authority.

Base is the exact personal main bf6c77b92246464b1e34177bc851d1ffc008c1b7, preserving accepted owning Sol1276955c86ff46936cd1ce7d81fbc790f7068e1e and all three merged personal worker/Node22/Clio histories. Whole plan retains every current owner gate: meaningful RED barrier against actual production TurnSession, independent steer/follow-up positives and negatives, zero-warning nonempty compiled tests, lint/contract/guard/planning regressions, server/native-Clio builds and isolated startup/SIGTERM where relevant. Historical monorepo test/lint commands are preserved and mapped to actual standalone owner scripts. No runtime/compiler/provider/cloud/deployment test is claimed by this docs-only change.

Preparation and separate full peer preserve all191 inherited Git entries and all31 historical root compatibility receipts; whole77 new paths comprise story/design plus .ημ evidence. All62 one-LF command captures,15 exact owning Git archives,2 native-bound external pinned archives and literal original Eta card are verified. Current immutable Receipt River154440 actual API admits new selected .ημ physical row1; historical root31 rows are unchanged and not blanket-qualified. Distinct private complete Git/runtime peer has no actionable product finding and separately validates its own two declared receipts. Preparation failures remain inspectable in their original audit history; source is unchanged. Local checks supply no native review approval/cohort or runtime qualification.

Publication is DRAFT, blocked, automatic merge off. All three exact pinned reusable review jobs refuse drafts; the read-only Node22 candidate workflow may still execute on drafts. This bounded static route does not qualify runner isolation, safe READY activation or actual secret visibility. Current native checks remain required. Review and lawful owning-board registration/Ready precede implementation; absent Sol board configuration remains visible. Development stays on the personal fork. Final qualified origin integration must happen through a separate release/deploy PR; this planning PR neither releases the fix nor closes Eta255.

pullRequest.title: Add federated actor identity and agent credentials
pullRequest.body:
Axxium now represents humans and agents as separate actor kinds, reserves the configured administrator email for verified Google sign-in, and lets administrators issue expiring, revocable agent credentials. A verified AT Protocol OAuth callback can sign in or link a hosted DID; reciprocal handle/DID resolution remains a lookup rather than an authentication grant.

The production image contains only runtime dependencies and the compiled server, while `open-hax/services` owns the PDS and ingress. Locally, Axxium and Knoxx run under PM2 with Google OIDC and the shared account manager.

Validation: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run boundary:check`, `npm run build`, and `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate` passed. The image built, and the public PDS OAuth flow returned a signed-in Axxium human actor through `https://axxium.promethean.rest`.

* **New Features**
  * Sign in with Google or an AT Protocol identity, and link an AT Protocol identity to an existing account.

pullRequest.title: fix(axxium): settle open-hax/axxium#30 round-3 Codex findings
pullRequest.body:
Fork-first fixes for the three Codex P2s that Codex opened on open-hax/axxium#30, against the promotion head `6fdce06`. Red is `d1117ec` and green is `72e81af`.

- **r4277636448 (PRRT_kwDOStXBnc6skeB0), recover concurrent DID-link uniqueness conflicts.** If inserting the link binding hits `idx_provider_bindings_subject`, `link-actor!` reloads the winning binding. When the winner is the same actor the link succeeds; when it's a different actor the response is 409, not a raw 502. Tests: `concurrent-link-by-same-actor-succeeds` and `concurrent-link-by-other-actor-is-409`.
- **r4277636452 (PRRT_kwDOStXBnc6skeB3), keep OAuth starts from evicting live state.** The SDK `stateStore` is now `new-oauth-state-store`, a bounded TTL Map that never evicts a live entry. At capacity it purges expired entries first, then refuses a new key with `state-store-full-error`, and `start!` maps that to 503. The `sessionStore` keeps the LRU store, because sessions are revoked right after binding. Tests: `live-authorization-state-is-never-evicted` and `start-at-capacity-is-503`.
- **r4277636461 (PRRT_kwDOStXBnc6skeB-), paginate the account-manager actor list.** The new `resources/public/actor-pages.js` `fetchAllActors` pages `/api/actors?limit=100&offset=…` until it gets a short page. It de-duplicates rows that shift between pages and is bounded at 1000 pages. Tests: `scripts/actor-pages.test.mjs` (node:test), now part of `npm test`.

Verification on `72e81af`:
- `npm test`: cljs 50 tests / 190 assertions, plus 4/4 node:test.
- Red on `d1117ec`: 2 failures and 1 error in cljs, plus ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for the node test.
- typecheck and build have 0 warnings; `boundary:check`, the deployment-boundary check and clj-kondo are all clean.

Async tests keep the AGENTS.md `async`/`done` + `.catch` wrappers; there are no bare `^:async` deftests.

* **New Features**

pullRequest.title: fix: settle open-hax/sol#2 promotion review findings
pullRequest.body:
Fork-first fix for the open review findings on the promotion PR open-hax/sol#2 (`promote/a93ab2a`). After this merges, `open-hax:promote/a93ab2a` fast-forwards to the new fork main and the #2 threads settle as Fixed.

## Findings addressed
| Finding | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| CodeRabbit [r4253314449](https://github.com/open-hax/sol/pull/2#discussion_r4253314449): require a gap for every integration point | Checker requires a keyword `:gap` with a nonempty name on every point. |
| CodeRabbit [r4253314461](https://github.com/open-hax/sol/pull/2#discussion_r4253314461): reject anchors that don't identify the integration point | `expected-integration-anchors` maps each path to its anchor, kept separate from the proposal. A proposal whose anchor doesn't match is rejected (e.g. `"ns"`). |
| CodeRabbit [r4253314473](https://github.com/open-hax/sol/pull/2#discussion_r4253314473): roll back only artifacts owned by the failed initialization | `open!` deletes the ledger only if this attempt created it, and the schema directory only if it didn't exist before. Cleanup errors are swallowed and the original error is rethrown. Reopen behavior is unchanged. |
| Codex [r4253317713](https://github.com/open-hax/sol/pull/2#discussion_r4253317713): configure Clio in every exported startup path | New `core/resolve-app-config` (enrich + `clio-store/ensure-configured!`) used by `register-app-routes!` (so `solPlugin` gets it too) and `start!`. A store that is already open (from `bootstrap!`) is reused, never reopened. |
| Codex [r4253317715](https://github.com/open-hax/sol/pull/2#discussion_r4253317715): validate compiler output in the Node runtime workflow | `scripts/compile-clean.sh` copies the evidence workflow's `compile_clean` (completion line for the target, 0 warnings, no WARNING lines, exit 0, nonempty artifact). `node22-runtime.yml` runs both builds through it. `scripts/compile-clean.test.mjs` (part of `test:guard`) runs the same reject fixtures and asserts that no workflow build line skips the guard. |
| CodeRabbit [r4330643687](https://github.com/open-hax/sol/pull/2#discussion_r4330643687): close the turn that the compensation path admitted | `emit-start-lifecycle!` now emits `:sol.turn/failed` before `:sol.run/failed` (the compensating emit admits the pending turn start on retry). Red `c3cf73b`, green `dc1e907`. |
| CodeRabbit review 5497127322 body nit (sol-clio-cutover.md version spacing) | Fixed. |

## Verification (local, Node 22)
- Red (old source, new tests): checker 5 failures (missing gap, wrong anchor); CLJS 3 failures + 2 errors (rollback leaves ledger/schema; exported seam has no `:clio/store`); guard test 1 failure on the old workflow (unguarded build).
- Green: `npm test` 143 tests / 540 assertions, 0 failures, 0 warnings (was 138/528). `npm run test:guard` 23/23. `bb scripts/check_review_worker_plan_test.clj` 11 tests / 21 assertions. `bb scripts/check-review-worker-plan.clj` passes. `npm run lint` 0 errors / 0 warnings. `compile-clean.sh` passes for both `server` and `clio-native` builds.

  * Ledger and schema paths cannot overlap, including through symlinks. Interrupted initialization can recover or roll back safely while preserving existing data.
  * Reopening requires existing, nonempty schema history; concurrent appends are coordinated to prevent conflicting writes.
  * Failed turn starts now close the turn before reporting run failure.

* **Build Improvements**
